heading.en: Six per cent for the future

hook.en: Back in the 1960s an education commission said India should spend 6 per cent of its GDP on education. Why so much, and what has been done since?
hook.kn: 1960ರ ದಶಕದಲ್ಲೇ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ಆಯೋಗವೊಂದು ಜಿಡಿಪಿಯ 6% ಶಿಕ್ಷಣಕ್ಕೆ ಖರ್ಚು ಮಾಡಬೇಕೆಂದಿತು. ಏಕೆ ಅಷ್ಟು, ನಂತರ ಏನಾಯಿತು?

objectives.en: Explain how education spending is measured

narration.en: Back in the 1960s an education commission said India should spend 6 per cent of its GDP on education. Why so much, and what has been done since?
narration.kn: 1960ರ ದಶಕದಲ್ಲೇ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ಆಯೋಗವೊಂದು ಜಿಡಿಪಿಯ 6% ಶಿಕ್ಷಣಕ್ಕೆ ಖರ್ಚು ಮಾಡಬೇಕೆಂದಿತು. ಏಕೆ ಅಷ್ಟು, ನಂತರ ಏನಾಯಿತು?

body.en: Government spending on education is expressed in two ways: as a percentage of total government expenditure, which shows the importance of education in the government's scheme of things, and as a percentage of GDP, which shows how much of the country's income is committed to education. The Education Commission (1964–66), known as the Kothari Commission, recommended spending at least 6 per cent of GDP on education.
body.kn: ಶಿಕ್ಷಣದ ಮೇಲಿನ ಸರ್ಕಾರದ ವೆಚ್ಚವನ್ನು ಒಟ್ಟು ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ವೆಚ್ಚದ ಶೇಕಡಾ ಮತ್ತು ಜಿಡಿಪಿಯ ಶೇಕಡಾ ಎಂದು ಎರಡು ರೀತಿ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಪಡಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಕೊಠಾರಿ ಆಯೋಗ (1964–66) ಜಿಡಿಪಿಯ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ 6% ಶಿಕ್ಷಣಕ್ಕೆ ಖರ್ಚು ಮಾಡಲು ಶಿಫಾರಸು ಮಾಡಿತು.

narration.en: Government spending on education is expressed in two ways: as a percentage of total government expenditure, which shows the importance of education in the government's scheme of things, and as a percentage of GDP, which shows how much of the country's income is committed to education. The Education Commission (1964–66), known as the Kothari Commission, recommended spending at least 6 per cent of GDP on education.
narration.kn: ಶಿಕ್ಷಣದ ಮೇಲಿನ ಸರ್ಕಾರದ ವೆಚ್ಚವನ್ನು ಒಟ್ಟು ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ವೆಚ್ಚದ ಶೇಕಡಾ ಮತ್ತು ಜಿಡಿಪಿಯ ಶೇಕಡಾ ಎಂದು ಎರಡು ರೀತಿ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಪಡಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಕೊಠಾರಿ ಆಯೋಗ (1964–66) ಜಿಡಿಪಿಯ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ 6% ಶಿಕ್ಷಣಕ್ಕೆ ಖರ್ಚು ಮಾಡಲು ಶಿಫಾರಸು ಮಾಡಿತು.

body.en: The Right to Education Act, 2009 made free and compulsory education a fundamental right of all children aged 6 to 14 years. The government also levies an education cess on Union taxes to fund elementary education. Education for all is still a goal to be fully achieved; the gender gap in literacy has narrowed; and higher education has fewer takers, while unemployment is often highest among the educated.
body.kn: ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ಹಕ್ಕು ಕಾಯ್ದೆ 2009 6 ರಿಂದ 14 ವರ್ಷದ ಎಲ್ಲ ಮಕ್ಕಳಿಗೆ ಉಚಿತ ಮತ್ತು ಕಡ್ಡಾಯ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣವನ್ನು ಮೂಲಭೂತ ಹಕ್ಕಾಗಿಸಿತು. ಎಲ್ಲರಿಗೂ ಶಿಕ್ಷಣ ಇನ್ನೂ ಪೂರ್ಣ ಸಾಧನೆಯಾಗಿಲ್ಲ; ಸಾಕ್ಷರತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಲಿಂಗ ಅಂತರ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗಿದೆ.

points.en: Education cess to fund elementary education

narration.en: The Right to Education Act, 2009 made free and compulsory education a fundamental right of all children aged 6 to 14 years. The government also levies an education cess on Union taxes to fund elementary education. Education for all is still a goal to be fully achieved; the gender gap in literacy has narrowed; and higher education has fewer takers, while unemployment is often highest among the educated.

problem.en: A country's GDP is ₹250 lakh crore and the government spends ₹11.5 lakh crore on education. Find education spending as a percentage of GDP and the shortfall from the Kothari target.

steps.en: Shortfall = 6 − 4.6 = 1.4 percentage points, i.e. 0.014 × 250 = ₹3.5 lakh crore.

answer.en: 4.6% of GDP; ₹3.5 lakh crore short of the 6% target.
